what: WaterSim GR4J vs airGR and HBV vs TUWmodel (independent Fortran codes run in R)

gr4j_vs_airGR.case: airGR help example (?RunModel_GR4J): basin L0123001, X1=257.238, X2=1.012, X3=88.235, X4=2.208; explicit initial stores S=0.3 X1, R=0.5 X3 on 1989-01-01, no warm-up, run to 1999-12-31

hbv_vs_TUWmodel.case: TUWmodel help example, lumped Vils (198 km2, Austria) 1976-2008, parameters of ?TUWmodel with the melt threshold Tm set to (Tr+Ts)/2 = 1 C (HBV-light has one threshold), routing off (bmax=1) or fixed (bmax=10)
hbv_vs_TUWmodel.note_response: The response routines differ by design: TUWmodel releases (S/k) exp(-1/k) per day and lets part of the percolation reach the lower-box outflow on the same day, in a different order; HBV-light (WaterSim) uses an explicit daily step (PERC, then Q0, Q1, Q2). WaterSim is given K = exp(-1/k)/k (the same daily release share). The triangular weights also differ (TUW: discrete half-day midpoints). So total runoff is compared by NSE/KGE/volume, not to round-off.
